newsitem.title: USA: CME LUMBER CLOSES LOWER AS CASH AGAIN WEAK.
newsitem.headline: CME LUMBER CLOSES LOWER AS CASH AGAIN WEAK.

text.p: Reports that the cash lumber market has again truned easier on reduced demand kept pressure on CME lumber futures at the close, traders said.
Lumber closed mostly $3.40 to $1.50 per tbf lower with September off most at $361.50 and November off $2.70 at $353.60 per tbf.

Although futures moved up from early lows on short covering, private reports of a return to slow cash trade pressured the market. Cheaper wood is already starting to show up after some cash strength Tuesday on increased fill-in business, traders said.

Production remains too large for the current amount of usage. Even though some mills have cut back on hours and others are rumored to be planning to reduce production, cash can only show strength one or two days a week, they said.

"All of these (mill) cutbacks signal just one thing, that they can't sell the amount that they are producing," said Curt Cunningham, President of Pacific Futures Trading. "There's too much product and too little demand."
